main_text.l: uâ Rhenus fluit: auriferis quâ diues arenis
urbidus Oceanum leni Tagus agmine pulsat:
t te Roma legat caput imperiumque malorum.
Tu vero, tu, Christe, faue, qui luminis imbre
undta fouës, feruas, s alis solidaque serenas
atitia, s castis renouas mortalia corda:
alme faue, s sanctis præsens allabere cœptis:
selefiique patrocinio mendacia contra
et sulgi rabiem, præsens monimenta tuorum
incifa his tabulis iam, ter rediuiua tuere,
Dueis late circum tua lux s gloria crescant.

ERgo pium ruisus repetito sulnere pectus
Saucius, indulges iusto, Herdesiane, doloti,
Amissa duplici nunc, orbus coniuge coniux:
Nec tibi se socium in lacrymas adiunget amicus?
Immo terrarum longum licet interuallum,
Et montes fluuiique setent nos corpore iungi,
Absit st, absentis seluti contemptor amici,
Non lacrymis lacrymas, non planctus planctibus

page.notes: Greek line "ϲωφρονιστικον" is a best reading of the printed title word; the poem's first line is printed as "Ergo". Several letters in the verse (e.g. "s" for et-sign, "sulnere") are uncertain and should be checked against the scan; the ampersand-like sign before "alis" and "gloria" is rendered as s. Heading level and caput are not given, as the page is a continuation of a Sylva.
